summary.text: The law of conservation of energy says the total energy of an isolated system stays constant over time.
Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed or transferred, as when the chemical energy in dynamite becomes motion, heat and sound.
The law rules out perpetual motion machines of the first kind and follows from the laws of physics not changing over time.

items.prompt: A ball rolls down one ramp and up a frictionless ramp of a different shape. How high does it rise?

options.label: To the height it started from, whatever the shape
Higher, since the gap adds extra speed
Lower, since a new shape takes away energy
To a height set by the second ramp's shape

items.explain: The height a moving body ascends on a frictionless surface equals the height it fell from and does not depend on the shape.

items.prompt: An inventor sells a wheel that supposedly spins forever and powers a house with no fuel or outside supply. Why should you doubt it?

options.label: Wheels always lose their shape over time
No system without an outside energy supply can deliver unlimited energy
Houses use more energy than any wheel could hold
Energy can only be made by burning something

items.explain: A consequence of conservation is that a perpetual motion machine of the first kind cannot exist.

items.prompt: A stick of dynamite explodes. You add up all the motion, position, heat and sound energy released. How does the total compare with the chemical energy lost?

options.label: It is a little smaller, since some energy is lost
It is much larger, since an explosion makes energy
It matches it exactly
It cannot be compared with a chemical measure

items.explain: All the released forms add up to the exact decrease of chemical energy.

items.prompt: A sealed box is a closed system. By what route can its total energy change?

options.label: Only by energy entering or leaving the box
By energy being created inside it
By energy slowly wearing out inside it
By its parts changing from one form to another

items.explain: For a closed system, the total energy can only change through energy entering or leaving.

items.prompt: Measurements of atomic nuclei show a missing amount of mass called a mass defect. What does this show?

options.label: Energy can never be measured in nuclei
Mass can be converted into energy
Mass is always preserved apart from energy
Nuclei create energy out of nothing

items.explain: Mass-energy equivalence means mass can be converted to energy and vice versa, observed in nuclear binding energy.

items.prompt: Suppose an experiment gave different results on Monday than on Friday. Which law would be in doubt?

options.label: The law that force has direction
The law that motion needs a force
Conservation of mass without energy
Conservation of energy

items.explain: Noether's theorem links energy conservation to the fact that the laws of physics do not change over time.

paragraphs.heading: The law
paragraphs.text: The law of conservation of energy says that the total energy of an isolated system stays the same over time. Energy is never made or destroyed; it only changes form or moves from one place to another. In a closed system, the total can change only when energy flows in or out.

paragraphs.heading: An example with dynamite
paragraphs.text: When a stick of dynamite explodes, its chemical energy becomes the kinetic energy of flying pieces. Add up everything released, the motion and potential energy of the pieces plus the heat and sound, and the sum matches exactly the chemical energy that was lost.

paragraphs.heading: Why it holds
paragraphs.text: Noether's theorem, together with the stationary-action principle, proves the law as a result of one fact: the laws of physics do not change over time. It follows that no perpetual motion machine of the first kind can exist. No system without an outside supply of energy can hand out an endless amount of it.

paragraphs.heading: Mass counts as energy
paragraphs.text: In classical physics, conserving energy and conserving mass were separate ideas. Special relativity links the two through E = mc², so science now treats mass and energy together as the conserved quantity. Mass can therefore turn into energy and back. This shows up in atomic nuclei, where a mass defect is measured in their binding energy.

paragraphs.heading: Edges of the law
paragraphs.text: Depending on how energy is defined, general relativity may break the law on the scale of the whole cosmos. In quantum mechanics, Noether's theorem applies to expected values, so a consistent violation is provably impossible. Whether single events that break conservation could happen or be seen is still debated.

paragraphs.heading: Early hints
paragraphs.text: Around 550 BCE Thales of Miletus already sensed that some underlying substance is conserved, though he thought it was water. Empedocles held that nothing comes to be or perishes; the four roots of earth, air, water and fire are only rearranged. In 1605 Simon Stevin solved several problems about objects at rest by assuming perpetual motion cannot happen.

paragraphs.heading: Galileo and Huygens
paragraphs.text: In 1639 Galileo studied an interrupted pendulum and noticed that a moving body rises to the same height it fell from. On a frictionless surface, that height does not depend on the surface's shape. In 1669 Christiaan Huygens reported that in collisions both the total momentum and the total kinetic energy were the same before and after.

paragraphs.heading: Balls dropped into clay
paragraphs.text: Émilie du Châtelet proposed and tested the idea that total energy is conserved and is something other than momentum. She repeated an experiment from 1722 by Willem 's Gravesande, dropping balls from different heights into soft clay. The dent each ball made showed its kinetic energy grew with the square of its speed, and the dent grew in step with the drop height. Newton and Voltaire had thought energy was proportional to velocity.
